text:
Construction is composable. A feature can build a draft like:

```text
reply_to(event)
react_to(event, "+")
article(title, body)
nip29_group_reply(group_id, event)
podcast_episode_publish(show_id, episode_id)
```

Then finalizers may add protocol-specific envelope details:
 [...] 5. Make `register_defaults` stop being the conceptual app path. There should be mandatory substrate plus explicit feature bundles. Social, DMs, zaps, longform are feature choices, not “defaults.”
 [...]   .feature(nip02_follow_list())
  .feature(nip51_lists())
  .feature(nip29_groups())
  .feature(search())
  .feature(home_feed())
  .feature(my_app_feature())
  .start()
```

A `Feature` is installed capability: actions, parsers, projections, query types, capability needs. It is not an open screen. `nmp-defaults` should become a library of named feature bundles, not a magic black box. [...] A `Feature` should be the main composition unit. It bundles:

- typed views/read models
- typed commands/writes
- subscription demand
- ingest parsers
- capability needs
- projection encoders [...] **What Developers Need To Know**
They should know:

- Which feature bundles their app installs.
- Which `LiveQuery` a screen opens.
- Which typed projection the screen renders.
- Which typed commands publish events.
- When to close query handles.
- When a query is default outbox-routed vs explicitly relay-pinned. [...] They should not need to know:

- `SnapshotRegistry`
- projection tiers
- muted observers
- replay shapes
- relay fanout details
- NIP-65 mailbox routing internals
- `open_interest` plumbing
- FlatBuffer sidecar mechanics
- cache/store replay mechanics

That is the simplification: **keep NMP’s internal correctness machinery, but make the app model small and explicit.** [...] The `Kernel` has become a god object. It owns store, relay state, projection registries, action ledger, publish engine, observers, auth, accounts, provenance, cache serves, pull cursors, lifecycle, and multiple side registries. Some state belongs there, but not as one enormous mental object. See [kernel/mod.rs](/Users/pablofernandez/Work/nostr-multi-platform/crates/nmp-core/src/kernel/mod.rs:227).

Projection delivery is directionally right, but too layered. Keep FlatBuffers. Do not keep the current level of registry/tick-observer/feed-author-provider/declaration/incremental/rev/manifest/sidecar choreography as an app-visible model. `SnapshotRegistry` is doing too many jobs at once: [snapshot_registry.rs](/Users/pablofernandez/Work/nostr-multi-platform/crates/nmp-core/src/kernel/snapshot_registry.rs:114). The native embed sidecar feedback loop is especially suspect because it decodes a just-emitted frame to create another projection for a later tick. [...] 4. Split `SnapshotRegistry` into real owners: projection registry, projection delivery contract, tick observers, feed-author helpers. Same facade, simpler internals. [...] Internal complexity is justified only if it protects a real invariant: replay-before-live, privacy, route provenance, bounded FFI, no polling, signer safety, teardown, or cross-platform consistency.
